answer: Sybil resistance comes from quadratic stake: at its zenith an agent locks an opal bond bound to one hardware key, then needs vouches from separate already-staked identities. Voting weight grows as the square root of stake, so tenfold influence costs a hundredfold capital. A flood of cloned keys forms a river of noise but no real weight, because each face needs its own bond and unrelated vouchers, and fraud slashes them. Cloning scales cost superlinearly.
